[RDSC.14.2.3] `file` is the source module's name. The compiler **must**
write, for the file it was asked to compile, the name [RCLI.1.9] gives the
input; for a library read from a search-path entry the invocation names
([LIMP.3.1.1]), the path it was read from, as that entry spells it; for a
library read from the bundled library ([RCLI.1.11]), `<stdlib>/` followed by
its path relative to the bundle's directory, its segments joined by `/`
(`<stdlib>/calendar.ds`, `<stdlib>/units/si.ds`), whatever directory the
compiler found the bundle in; and for a module handed to the compiler with no
path, a synthetic name in angle brackets (`<in-memory:lib.ds>`). The name is an
input to the artefact ([RDSC.3.11]): the same library under a search-path entry
spelled differently has another name, and a bundled library has one name
wherever the compiler is installed.
The compiler emits one `DsSource` atom per source module; the
`DsSource`'s `module_id` is the per-module join key it shares with
every other atom belonging to the same module ([RDSC.4.7]).
